title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving emergency preventive and curative services in Wanlaweyn District Lower Shabelle region.

description.narrative: ltpgtPeace Development Action (PDA) proposes a nine-month nutrition project to combat acute malnutrition in Wanlaweyn District, Somalia, targeting vulnerable populations in the villages of ltbrgtDa'ud Bulle, Tabelaha , Hero , Hakow, Doonka, Maynuun and Waberi . These areas face chronic food insecurity driven by recurrent droughts, conflict, and limited healthcare access. The project aligns with Somalia’s 2024 Reserve Allocation Strategy, emphasizing anticipatory and early-response interventions to mitigate the projected impacts of La Niña-induced climatic shocks, which are expected to worsen malnutrition and food insecurity.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will focus on detecting, treating, and preventing malnutrition through two core components of Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM): community mobilization and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP). Activities will adhere to Somalia’s IMAM protocols and Ministry of Health (MoH) guidelines, ensuring compliance with national standards. PDA will coordinate closely with area-based coordination groups and key stakeholders, fostering synergies with health, WASH, and protection partners to strengthen referral pathways and enhance service delivery. This integrated approach will improve access to care and maximize the project’s impact across all target communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtCommunity Health Workers (CHWs) will conduct regular malnutrition screenings using the Family MUAC approach, empowering caregivers to measure their children’s MUAC at home. This community-based method facilitates early detection of malnutrition, enabling timely treatment and reducing the risk of severe outcomes. Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) cases will be managed through a fixed-site TSFP and two outreach sites. Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases will be referred to OTP sites managed by other cluster partners.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo prevent malnutrition, the project will promote maternal, infant, and young child nutrition (MIYCN) practices through community-based sessions led by IYCF counselors and MTMSGs. These sessions will educate families on exclusive breastfeeding, complementary feeding, and dietary diversity, engaging both men and women to ensure widespread household adoption of optimal feeding practices. These preventive strategies will play a critical role in improving child nutrition and reducing malnutrition rates in the long term. Household nutrition and resilience will be further supported through nutrition-sensitive agriculture initiatives such as kitchen gardening and poultry farming. Kitchen gardening, using household water for irrigation, will enable families to cultivate nutrient-rich vegetables, improving access to fresh, diverse foods. The "One Egg Per Child Per Day" initiative, delivered through Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA), will provide resources for small-scale poultry farming, ensuring sustainable access to protein-rich foods like eggs. These interventions will improve dietary diversity and strengthen household food security, key factors in mitigating the impacts of recurrent droughts and food shortages. Additionally, the project will distribute micronutrient supplements to children under five, addressing critical deficiencies in Vitamin A, iron, and folic acid. These supplements will boost immunity and promote healthy growth, complementing the broader nutrition strategy to reduce severe malnutrition risks.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtPDA will uphold Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) by incorporating community feedback mechanisms into project implementation, ensuring transparency and adaptability to local needs. The project will also integrate Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention, Child Protection, and Prevention of Aid Diversion (PDAD) measures across all activities. By working closely with local leaders and community groups, PDA will ensure that all services are delivered safely, equitably, and with dignity, prioritizing the protection of women and children.ltbrgtlt/pgt
